warrant: The graded observable is the energy-minimized BSR prolongator's nonzero entries on a linear-elasticity operator, compared under atol 1e-12 plus rtol 1e-10 after the immutable test_incomplete_mat_mult_bsr case passes. Physical: a wrong block-sparse incomplete matrix product in incomplete_mat_mult_bsr (pyamg/amg_core/smoothed_aggregation.h:970), reached through energy_prolongation_smoother's BSR path (pyamg/aggregation/smooth.py:875), fails the gate's own gold-reference comparison on synthetic matrices or changes many prolongator block entries far beyond this bound on a realistic operator. Achievable: the tentative prolongator and strength matrix are built once, deterministically, before B is perturbed, so only floating-point operation ordering inside the block-sparse product and CG energy minimization sets legitimate sensitivity. Aggregate numbering is storage, not physics: `standard_aggregation` numbers aggregates by the order in which it scans rows (pyamg/aggregation/aggregate.py:12) and a correct implementation that groups the same degrees of freedom may number them differently, exactly as the leaf's aggregate-* checks already assume. The probe therefore puts the aggregates in a canonical order -- each keyed by the smallest fine index it holds, an identity the output itself carries -- and re-sorts the sparse indices before reading the data array, so no graded value is keyed by an aggregate number. Self-tested against a renumbered reference, as the skill's pointwise-grades-physics rule requires: with `standard_aggregation`'s output columns permuted at random -- the same aggregates, numbered differently -- the graded array moves by 1.38e-14 (worst bound_fraction 4.63e-03), against 0.22 when the raw numbering is graded.
